qs.stem: A cyclist rides to a studio at 36 km/h and returns by the same road at 45 km/h. What is the average speed for the whole trip, in km/h?
steps: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time, not the average of the two speeds.
Take the one-way distance as 180 km (a number both speeds divide).
Average = 40 km/h.
qs.trap: Taking (36 + 45) ÷ 2 = 40.5. More time is spent at the slower speed.

steps: Look at the gaps between terms first; if they do not settle, try multiplying, squares, or two series taking turns.

Answer: 30.

qs.stem: A child climbs a staircase of 8 steps, taking either 1 or 2 steps at a time. In how many different ways can the child reach the top?
steps: To reach step k, the last move came from step k − 1 or step k − 2, so ways(k) = ways(k − 1) + ways(k − 2).
ways(1) = 1, ways(2) = 2.
Answer: 34.

qs.stem: Riya can paint a mural in 15 days. Arjun can paint the same mural in 30 days. Working together at these rates, how many days will they take?
steps: In one day Riya does 1/15 of the job and Arjun does 1/30.
Together: 1/15 + 1/30 = 1/10 of the job per day.
Answer: 10 days.
qs.trap: Averaging the two times. Working together is always faster than the faster person alone.

qs.stem: What is the smaller angle, in degrees, between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 7:15?
steps: The minute hand moves 6° per minute: at 15 minutes it is at 15 × 6 = 90°.
The hour hand moves 30° per hour plus 0.5° per minute: 7 × 30 + 15 × 0.5 = 217.5°.
The smaller angle is 127.5°.
qs.trap: Leaving the hour hand exactly on the hour. It moves on as the minutes pass.

qs.stem: Which of these make a standing lamp less likely to tip over?
opts: Making the base narrower
A wider base
A lower centre of gravity
Moving heavy parts higher up
steps: An object tips when its centre of gravity moves outside its base.
A wide base gives more room before that happens.
A heavy base lowers the centre of gravity.
Moving weight upwards raises the centre of gravity and makes it less stable.
Correct: A wider base; A lower centre of gravity. Not correct: Making the base narrower; Moving heavy parts higher up.
qs.trap: Thinking height adds strength. Height makes tipping easier.

qs.stem: Which of these make long paragraphs easier to read?
opts: Lines of roughly 45 to 75 characters
Comfortable line spacing
Very light grey text on white
Strong contrast between text and background
steps: Readable text needs good contrast and enough line spacing.
Very long lines make it hard to find the next line; very short lines break the flow.
All capitals remove the word shapes we rely on, so they slow reading.
So contrast, spacing and moderate line length help.
Correct: Lines of roughly 45 to 75 characters; Comfortable line spacing; Strong contrast between text and background. Not correct: Very light grey text on white.
qs.trap: Thinking capitals are clearer. They work for short labels, not paragraphs.

qs.stem: Which of these depend on air pressure to work?
opts: Drawing medicine into a syringe
A spring weighing scale
A catapult launching a stone
A rubber suction hook on tiles
steps: When you suck on a straw, the air pressure inside drops and outside air pressure pushes the juice up.
A suction hook is held by outside air pressing on it.
Pulling a syringe plunger lowers the pressure inside so liquid is pushed in.
A catapult uses stored elastic energy.
Correct: Drawing medicine into a syringe; A rubber suction hook on tiles. Not correct: A spring weighing scale; A catapult launching a stone.
qs.trap: Thinking you "pull" the liquid up. Outside air pressure pushes it.

qs.stem: Why is a door handle fitted on the edge farthest from the hinges?
opts: A longer distance from the hinge gives more turning effect for the same push
The door is lightest at that edge
It keeps the handle away from dust
The hinges cannot hold a handle nearby
steps: Turning effect (moment) = force × distance from the pivot.
The hinges are the pivot.
Pushing far from the hinge gives the biggest moment.
So the door opens with the least effort. (Option A.)
qs.trap: Ignoring the pivot. Try pushing a door near its hinges: it is much harder.

qs.stem: In a certain non-leap year, 1 January is a Friday. What day of the week is 10 October in that year?
opts: Sunday
Thursday
Monday
Friday
steps: 282 = 7 × 40 + 2, so the weekday moves on by 2.
Friday + 2 days = Sunday.
Answer: Sunday.
qs.trap: Counting 1 January itself as a day to move on. Start from day 0.

qs.stem: In the "rule of thirds" for photography, where should the main subject usually be placed?
opts: Exactly in the centre of the frame
At the very edge of the frame
In the bottom third only
Along the lines that divide the frame into thirds, or where they cross
steps: Imagine two horizontal and two vertical lines dividing the frame into nine equal parts.
Placing the subject on these lines or their crossings usually gives a more balanced, lively picture.
Horizons often go on the upper or lower third line.
It is a guideline, not a strict law. (Option D.)
qs.trap: Thinking the centre is always best.

qs.stem: The sitar belongs to which group of instruments?
opts: Percussion instruments
Wind instruments
String instruments
Keyboard instruments
steps: The sitar has plucked playing strings and extra strings that vibrate in sympathy.
Its sound comes from vibrating strings.
Tabla is percussion; bansuri and shehnai are wind instruments.
Answer: string instruments. That is option C.
qs.trap: Choosing percussion because it is often played with the tabla.

qs.stem: Bandhani, popular in Gujarat and Rajasthan, is a technique of:
opts: Weaving silk with gold thread
Embroidering with mirrors
Printing with carved wooden blocks
Tie-dyeing cloth by tying tiny knots before dyeing
steps: In Bandhani, small points of cloth are pinched and tied tightly with thread.
The tied parts resist the dye.
When untied, they leave patterns of dots.
Answer: tie-dyeing. That is option D.
qs.trap: Confusing it with block printing.

qs.stem: Why does food cook faster in a pressure cooker?
opts: The higher pressure raises the boiling point of water above 100 °C
Steam carries less heat than boiling water
The higher pressure lowers the boiling point of water
The sealed lid stops all heat from escaping
steps: Water boils when its vapour pressure matches the pressure above it.
Sealing the cooker raises the pressure inside.
So water boils at about 120 °C instead of 100 °C.
Hotter water cooks food faster. (Option A.)
qs.trap: Thinking pressure lowers the boiling point. That happens on mountains, where pressure is lower.

opts: It increases the force needed
It doubles the distance the flag moves
It halves the force needed
It changes the direction of the force without reducing it
steps: A fixed pulley does not move with the load.

The force needed stays the same as the flag's weight (ignoring friction).
Its benefit is convenience: you pull down instead of climbing. (Option D.)

qs.stem: In a monospaced font, which statement is true?
opts: Only capital letters are allowed
Every character takes up the same width
Letters have no serifs
Every character has the same height
steps: In most fonts an "i" is much narrower than an "m".
A monospaced font gives every character the same width.
This keeps columns aligned, so it is used for code and old typewriters.
Monospaced fonts can have serifs (like Courier). (Option B.)
qs.trap: Thinking monospaced means sans-serif.
